# Reading data from the web 

Two major paths: 

* data included as content on a webpage, and you want to "Scrape" those data 

  * table from Wikipedia 
  * reviews from Amazon 
  * cast and characters on IMBD 

* There's a dedicated server holding data in a relatively usable form, and you want to ask for those data 

  * open NYC data 
  * Data.gov 
  * Star Wars API 
  
## Scraping web content 

* Webpages combine HTML (content) and CSS (styling) to produce what you see. 
* When you retrieve the HTML for a page with data you want, you've retrieved the data. 
* There's also a lot of other stuff, so the challenge is extracting what you want from HTML

CSS Selectors 

* because CSS controls appearances, CSS identifiers appear throughout HTML code 
* HTML elemets you care about frequently have unique identifiers 
* extracting what you want from HTML is often a question of selecting against CSS tags 
* To do this, use Selector Gadget
  * in a browser, go to page you care about and launch Selector Gadget 
  * click on thinks you want, unclick what you don't 
  
Scraping data into R 

* rvest facilitates web scraping 
* workflow 
  * download HTML using read_html()
  * extract elements using html_elements() and CSS selector 
  * extract HTMl stuff you want 
  
## APIs 

* Application Programming Interfaces provide a way to communicate with the software 
* web APIs may give you a way to request specific data from a server 
* web APIs not uniform 
* this means that what is returned by one API will differ from what is returned by another API 
* often either get CSV or Java Script Object Notation (JSON) (extremely common data format) 

Getting data from the web is messy! 

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(rvest)
library(httr)
```

# Extracting tables 

```{r}
url = "https://www.samhsa.gov/data/sites/default/files/NSDUHsaeShortTermCHG2015/NSDUHsaeShortTermCHG2015.htm" 

drug_use_html = 
  read_html(url)
```

## Pull the tables out 

```{r}
drug_use_html |> 
  html_table()
```

```{r}
marj_df = 
  drug_use_html |> 
  html_table() |> 
  first () |> #first element of list to pull out
  slice(-1) #subtract out the first row, got rid of the NOTE row 
```
There's a lot of tidying to do, but we'll figure that out next class 

## Import some Star Wars data

Pull in the HTML 
read_html_live is experimental package, uses Chrome in the background 
This was not working - update R, install chromote 
```{r}
swm_html = 
  read_html_live("https://www.imdb.com/list/ls070150896/")
```

selector gadget 

```{r}
swm_title_vec = 
  swm_html |> 
  html_elements(".ipc-title-link-wrapper .ipc-title__text") |> 
  html_text() #just gives text from 

swm_metascore_vec = 
  swm_html |> 
  html_elements(".metacritic-score-box") |> 
  html_text() 

swm_runtime_vec = 
  swm_html |> 
  html_elements(".ipc-inline-list__item:nth-child(2)") |> 
  html_text() 

```

```{r}
swm_df = 
  tibble(
    title = swm_title_vec, 
    score = swm_metascore_vec, 
    runtime = swm_runtime_vec
  )
```

## NYC water using API 
Getting a CSV 
```{r}
nyc_water_df = 
  GET("https://data.cityofnewyork.us/api/v3/views/ia2d-e54m/query.csv") |> 
  content("parsed") |>  #take a guess and pull out what you think I want
  select(year:per_capita_gallons_per_person_per_day)
```
Go to export on website --> API endpoint --> CSV --> copy API endpoint 
You should really only import HTML once, that process is not free. separate out that part of the code 

Getting a JSON file - CSV is better if there's an option for it 
```{r}
nyc_water_json = 
  GET("https://data.cityofnewyork.us/api/v3/views/ia2d-e54m/query.json") 

nyc_water_json |> 
  content("text") |> 
  jsonlite::fromJSON() |> 
  as_tibble() |> 
  select(year:per_capita_gallons_per_person_per_day)
```

Look at Pokemon! 

```{r}
pokemon_json = 
  GET("https://pokeapi.co/api/v2/pokemon/1")
```

Extracting data from JSON file about the first pokemon (bulbasaur)
```{r}
pokemon_data = 
  pokemon_json |> 
  content()

pokemon_data[["name"]]
pokemon_data[["height"]]
pokemon_data[["abilities"]]

```
